newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong red chips sizzle on handover euphoria.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong red chips sizzle on handover euphoria.

text.p: Hong Kong-incorporated companies with mainland financial backing, or red chips, pushed ahead on Thursday afternoon on euphoria over the territory's handover to China on July 1, analysts said.
The Hang Seng China-affiliated Corporations Index hit a record high of 3,291.22 before easing to 3,239, up 54 points, or 1.70 percent.
"Investors are buying on handover fever," said Franco Tong, institutional sales manager at New China Hong Kong Securities.
But the gains were focused on several heavyweight and good quality red chips, he added.

"The rally on red chips is virtually a pre-handover fever and some may worry the recent rise will be a bit overdone, but I am still confident on their prospects for the rest of the year," said Raymond Jook, associate director of China research at SocGen Crosby.
China Everbright-IHD surged HK$2.55 to HK$22.80 and China Merchants added HK$2.25 to HK$23.40.
